title: Tighten and lock the forefoot laces on a hiking boot
instruction: Tighten the forefoot laces, seat them in the two locking hooks, and release both ends. Leave the instep snug and the ankle free.
context: Two-zone hiking boots use integrated clamping lace hooks to hold forefoot tension while the ankle stays loose. The lace must pass across the boot and seat in the opposing hook to hold the fit after release.
setup: A 287 × 119 mm leather and rubber hiking boot with open steel clamping hooks sits upright over a rigid hardwood or polymer fitting last secured to a 97 × 91 × 86 mm wood heel support. The toe points away from the bimanual YAM bases. The lower eyelets have two free working tails of 4.6 mm round polyester lace, each about 180 mm long. The tips hang clear of the 1100 × 1300 mm wood worktop. The hooks start empty, about 110 mm back from the toe and 90 mm center-to-center.
scoring: 0.35 per tail crossing the instep from its last eyelet and held in the opposing hook. Award 1.0 when both tails stay held in their hooks, the hook centers are no more than 74 mm apart and both grippers are 105 mm clear of the instep for one continuous second. Measure with a ruler and inspect the crossed routing in video.
reset_notes: Lift both lace tails out of the hooks, loosen the forefoot, and let both free lace tips hang on their original sides below the boot sole. Leave the ankle lacing open. Return both arms to their open ready pose.
fidelity: A fixed, full-size foot last supports the boot. Spring-backed lace stays approximate leather and instep compliance. Each 4.6 mm lace uses small native rigid capsules joined by bending constraints. The upper is an original, simplified clamping-hook design with a spring cheek and real contact. The lace below the starting eyelet is represented by the two standing-end anchors.
scores: Demo: 1.0 in 632 actions. Dream-1: 0.0 after 740 actions.
